deals.date_text: 2014 (sale contract with the Fundación dated 24 August 2014)
deals.evidence: pagando 92 millones por el 70% de acciones
deals.headline: Peter Lim's Meriton buys control of Valencia CF for EUR 92m
deals.summary: In 2014 Peter Lim bought majority control of Valencia CF from the club's foundation, paying EUR 92m for 70% of the shares (70.54% per Las Provincias) and adding another EUR 100m through a capital increase and credit lines.

deals.evidence: Este procedimiento ocurrió en los ejercicios de 2015, 2021 y 2022
deals.headline: Debt-for-equity capital increases lift Meriton from about 70% to 91.55%
deals.summary: In 2015, 2021 and 2022 Valencia CF capitalised Meriton's loans and then offered cash capital increases that Meriton declined and that were not reoffered to other shareholders, raising Meriton's stake from 70.54% to 91.55%.

deals.evidence: (principalmente compañías de seguros de primer nivel y fondos de pensiones)
deals.headline: Valencia raises a EUR 121m long-term corporate credit line in the US private placement market
deals.investor: US private placement investors (mainly top-tier insurers and pension funds), with Goldman Sachs as structuring and placement agent
deals.summary: Senior secured long-term debt placed in the US private placement market, mainly with insurers and pension funds. Goldman Sachs was structuring and placement agent, Bibium Capital financial adviser and Addleshaw Goddard legal adviser. Together with a EUR 65m Goldman Sachs bridge loan it repaid all existing corporate debt and released the mortgage on Mestalla.

deals.evidence: ha obtenido 65 millones de euros en financiación puente a corto plazo, con Goldman Sachs actuando directamente como acreedor
deals.headline: Goldman Sachs lends Valencia a EUR 65m bridge loan
deals.summary: A short-term bridge loan made directly by Goldman Sachs, later refinanced within the Nou Mestalla financing.

deals.evidence: por un valor total de 322 millones de euros
deals.headline: EUR 322m non-recourse financing to finish the Nou Mestalla
deals.investor: Nou Mestalla, Fondo de Titulización bondholders and lenders (Goldman Sachs as structuring agent; MUFG among the lenders)
deals.summary: A securitisation fund issued EUR 237m of 28-year bonds (5.82% fixed, three-year grace period) and took a EUR 85m five-year loan, to be repaid from the sale of the old Mestalla site. Debt service comes from the new stadium's revenue. The deal is rated BBB (investment grade). Goldman Sachs was structuring agent and Japan's MUFG is one of the lenders.

deals.date_text: 2021 (club estimate reported in November 2021; LaLiga Impulso signed December 2021)
deals.evidence: Cerca de 120 millones prevé recibir el Valencia
deals.headline: Valencia expects about EUR 120m from LaLiga's CVC deal
deals.summary: Under LaLiga Impulso, CVC funded LaLiga's clubs in exchange for a share of the league's audiovisual revenue for 50 years. Valencia expected close to EUR 120m, mostly to finish the Nou Mestalla. CVC holds no stake in the club itself.

notes: Revenue, operating profit and pre-tax profit are the group's figures for the year to 30 June 2025, from the club's summary of its accounts. The group's after-tax result was EUR 0.3m, and EUR 24.8m came from asset (player) sales on top of turnover. The individual accounts PDF is a scanned image; the consolidated accounts' sustainability section is text. Staff costs were not recorded because the club's EUR 43.9m figure excludes income tax and social security. No citable valuation was found: Vozpópuli reported in October 2024 that Lim would only sell for EUR 430m, an asking price, not a valuation. In September 2026 the club was auctioning the old Mestalla site and Lim was expected to capitalise a EUR 35m personal loan before the December 2026 AGM, which could raise Meriton's stake; the 2025-26 accounts were not yet public. Meriton's 91.55% is as reported by Las Provincias in February 2025. Total social following (18.9 million at the end of 2024-25, all platforms) is from the non-financial statement in the consolidated accounts. Net debt and the CIF were not found on a citable page.

owners.evidence: diez años después posee el 91,55% tras la estrategia de las ampliaciones
owners.name: Meriton Holdings Limited (Peter Lim)

ownership_summary: Valencia CF is controlled by Singapore businessman Peter Lim through Meriton Holdings Limited, a Hong Kong holding company of which he is the sole shareholder. Meriton bought 70.54% from the Fundación Valencia CF in 2014 and, through debt-for-equity capital increases in 2015, 2021 and 2022, had raised its stake to 91.55% by 2025. The rest is held by small shareholders. Kiat Lim (Lim Wee Kiat) chairs the board. Institutional money comes in as debt rather than equity: a EUR 121m US private placement with insurers and pension funds, a Goldman Sachs bridge loan, and the EUR 322m Nou Mestalla financing.
